name: Amsterdam
tagline: Canal-Laced Charm, World-Class Cycling, and Liberal Dutch Design Culture
description: Amsterdam combines 17th-century canal beauty with cutting-edge design, a famously tolerant culture, and one of the world's most bike-friendly urban environments. Nearly everyone speaks excellent English, the healthcare system is superb, and the compact city size means everything is accessible by bicycle. Housing is expensive and competitive, but the quality of life — anchored by cycling, culture, and gezelligheid — is exceptional.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day Schengen visa-free for US citizens. DAFT treaty allows US citizens to obtain self-employed residency. No dedicated retirement visa — most retirees use tourist visa renewals or the orientation year permit.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Safe — low violent crime; watch for bicycle theft and tourist-area pickpocketing
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (AMS) — 20 min from city center by train
quickFacts.climate: Maritime temperate with cool summers (17-22°C) and cold, damp winters (1-6°C). Frequent wind, cloud cover, and rain year-round.

housing.description: Compact studio in Amsterdam-Noord, Nieuw-West, or Zuidoost, outside the canal ring but connected by ferry and metro

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with occasional budget eats out

healthcare.description: Entry private/international plan pitched at the residence-permit requirement

transportation.description: Bike plus pay-as-you-go OV for occasional trams; no car

1M.lifestyle: A compact studio in Amsterdam-Noord, Nieuw-West, or Zuidoost, outside the canal ring but a quick ferry or metro ride from the centre. Days run on a bike with pay-as-you-go transit for the occasional tram, and most meals are cooked at home with the odd Surinamese, Turkish, or Indonesian plate out. Health cover is an entry private/international plan pitched at the visa requirement. The apartment is modest and dining out is rationed, but Amsterdam's cycling culture, the Vondelpark, free ferries across the IJ, and canal-side afternoons keep daily life rich for very little.

housing.description: Larger studio or small 1-bedroom in Noord, Oost, or De Baarsjes

dining.description: Eating out roughly weekly, mix of budget and mid-range

healthcare.description: Private/international plan plus a supplementary layer (dental/physio)

transportation.description: GVB Vrij unlimited monthly pass (€129) plus bike

2M.lifestyle: A larger studio or small one-bedroom in Noord, Oost, or De Baarsjes, with an unlimited GVB transit pass alongside the bike. Eating out becomes roughly weekly, health cover adds a supplementary layer for dental and physiotherapy, and there is room for a standard gym and regular culture. It is unshowy, comfortable city living below the canal-ring premium — enough slack for a good social rhythm without stretching.

housing.description: Modern 1-bedroom in a solid residential district (Oost, Westerpark, De Baarsjes), around the city average, nicely furnished

healthcare.description: Comprehensive individual international plan (~Cigna Silver class)

transportation.description: GVB Vrij pass plus bike; no car

entertainment.description: Mid/premium gym plus concerts, museums, nightlife

3M.lifestyle: A modern one-bedroom in a solid residential district like Oost, Westerpark, or De Baarsjes, around the city average and nicely furnished. Dining out is a regular habit, health cover steps up to a comprehensive international plan, and the GVB pass plus bike cover everything without a car. Museums, concerts, and Amsterdam nightlife are freely accessible, with real budget margin left each month — the classic comfortable-retirement tier in an expensive but livable city.

housing.description: Spacious 1-bedroom or modest 2-bedroom in a prime central district — De Pijp, Oud-Zuid, or the Jordaan

healthcare.description: Premium international plan (Cigna Gold / Allianz Care comprehensive)

transportation.description: GVB Vrij pass, bike, regular taxis, occasional car hire

entertainment.description: Premium gym plus theatre, events, hobbies

luxuryExtras.description: Club memberships, fine wine, short-haul travel fund, concierge extras

5M.lifestyle: A spacious one-bedroom or modest two-bedroom in a prime central district — De Pijp, Oud-Zuid, or the Jordaan — with a weekly cleaner handling the flat. Dining is frequent and often high-end, a premium international health plan removes friction, and transport adds regular taxis or an occasional hire car on top of the pass and bike. A premium gym, theatre, and a short-haul travel fund round it out — upper-affluent living in one of Europe's most desirable cities.

housing.description: Grand canal-house apartment in the Grachtengordel or Oud-Zuid, or a Zuidas luxury penthouse

healthcare.description: Top-tier international concierge (Cigna Platinum / Bupa Global elite), worldwide, evacuation

transportation.description: Leased/owned car (incl. Amsterdam parking premium) plus taxis and the GVB pass

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeper several times a week (~50 hrs/mo @ ~€18–20/hr)

luxuryExtras.description: Concierge, wine cellar, premium memberships, discretionary travel

10M.lifestyle: A grand canal-house apartment in the Grachtengordel or Oud-Zuid, or a Zuidas luxury penthouse, kept by a housekeeper several times a week. Dining is near-daily at the city's best tables, health cover is top-tier international concierge with worldwide access, and a leased car sits alongside the pass and bike for when the canals don't suit. The discretionary budget funds club memberships, a wine cellar, concierge services, and regular travel. This is the top of what the city offers short of buying a canal house outright — a trophy address, staff on hand, and Amsterdam's culture fully open.
